clips.caption:
Every manifesting technique, every goal-setting method, every success program you've ever paid for runs through the same filter: your habits.

You can't just stop a habit. You can't will it away through sheer discipline either - try that and it comes back harder. The only way out is to replace it with something else, on purpose, every single time it fires.

Winning is a habit. Losing is a habit. Neither one is who you are - it's just what you've practiced.

Successful people aren't smarter in the moment. They just have a different script running.

clips.start_words: Two different parts of the brain
clips.caption:
Breaking a habit isn't a willpower problem. It's a chemistry problem.

Every habit, good or bad, is biologically addictive - the brain floods you with dopamine and serotonin when you do it, the same reward system that lights up on a drug. Stop doing it and the brain makes you feel anxious and bad until you go back to it. That's not weakness. That's the exact design of addiction.

You can't out-discipline a chemical loop. You can only replace it with one that pays you the same hit.

clips.start_words: I'll tell you an interesting story
clips.end_words: half an hour to my new house
clips.caption:
He moved out of his old house. Weeks later, he drove home from a meeting downtown and pulled into the driveway - of the house he didn't live in anymore.

No thought involved. His body just ran the old route, because the route was never a decision in the first place. It was a habit, repeated enough times that it stopped needing him to be present at all.

Most of your day runs the exact same way. The question is just which routes you've let become automatic.

There's a one-word trick for catching a habit before it runs you.

First, you'll notice a day later that you did the old habit again - say "cancel, cancel" anyway, just to mark it. Keep going and you'll start catching it the same day, then in the middle of doing it, then right before you're about to do it. Every single time, just say it: cancel, cancel.

Eventually you catch it before it starts, and that's the whole game - not willpower, just noticing sooner.
